vo: Your customers now buy integrated solutions. But decades of autonomy built leaders for silos. That is the gap.
Enterprise leadership is not a job title. A leader may run a single unit, and still decide for the economic and social welfare of the whole firm.
First, focus. Complexity pulls attention inward, to structure and process. Enterprise leaders prioritize ruthlessly, and keep only what creates differentiated value for the customer.
Second, build. Enterprise leaders develop strategic competence, what the firm can do, and organizational character, who it is, at the same time.
Third, reconcile. Cost against growth. Stability against reinvention. Enterprise leaders look at their own company as a stranger would, and hold both sides.

Fourth, align. Meaning: a shared reason to integrate. Mind-set: the beliefs people bring to work. Mobilization: processes that move people and resources. Measurement: what gets counted and rewarded. And mechanisms for renewal, so the system never settles.
Yet it remains an unnatural act. Cultures celebrate unit heroes, frameworks reward isolated expertise, and pay follows unit results.
So build them on purpose. Demand an enterprise view, and measure it, from the top. Rotate high potentials across the firm. Track talent across silos.
Integrated solutions need leaders who act for the whole.
